evidence.note: Scans for package.json/vite/webpack build-tool artifacts (anti-cheat rule 2) early, right around initial build — treating the no-build-pipeline gate as a fatal constraint to check upfront.
curl -fsSL the three exact upstream lib URLs into /app/static/ flat paths — pristine download to exact pinned versions/paths, the canonical way to satisfy the hash gate.

sha256sum of the three vendored libs recomputed four times, including after each DB-wipe rebuild — verifying the hash gate rather than assuming it, and guarding against regression as the build evolves.
find -size +30M -perm /111 audits the no-vendored-binary anti-cheat surface (rule 3).
Repeats the lockfile/config artifact scan late in the build, re-confirming the build-tool gate held.
grep -c 'class="status"' on / to confirm the seeded-status minimum gate is met, re-checked after rebuild.

reasoning: The agent explicitly triaged and front-loaded the cheap-but-fatal gates — pristine vendoring to exact paths (step 10), repeated hash recomputation (19/64/71/88), anti-cheat binary and build-tool scans (7/18/62/63/89), and seed-minimum counts (70/87) — and verified rather than assumed each, re-checking after rebuilds to guard against regression, which squarely matches the level-8 anchor. It falls short of level 10 because I see no explicit palette measurement, dedicated CSP-header scan, or offline-runtime confirmation. The score is not higher because the gate audit, while systematic on hashes/anti-cheat/seed, does not cover the full binary-gate surface with concrete proofs.
